title.narrative: From Communities to Policy: Strengthening Local and Transboundary Action for Water Rights

description.narrative: This project is part of a long-standing diocesan pastoral and social commitment to accompany vulnerable communities and defend human dignity. It addresses ongoing challenges related to unequal access to safe water, the deterioration of community water systems, weak local governance, and the limited recognition of water as a fundamental human right. These challenges disproportionately affect poor rural communities, especially women, children and families living in vulnerable conditions. Building on the strong diocesan presence and close relationships with local communities, the project places the human right to water at the centre of its approach, combining technical support, community organisation and rights-based action, rooted in participation and pastoral accompaniment. Through parish and diocesan structures, the project strengthens local water committees and community organisations responsible for water management. It promotes inclusive, transparent and accountable governance, encouraging shared responsibility and active participation, with particular attention to women and marginalised groups. The project also raises awareness of water as a human right and of the responsibilities linked to its use and protection. Communities are supported to understand legal and institutional frameworks, to engage peacefully with authorities and service providers, and to advocate for their rights in an informed and organised way. By integrating faith-based accompaniment, rights-based action and environmental stewardship, the project aims to contribute to lasting improvements in dignity, well-being and social cohesion.
